findings.summary: Established simulators do not assign one universal input policy to the phrase absolute refractory. Brian 2 can freeze selected state variables while allowing others to evolve; NEST iaf_psc_delta discards refractory input by default or can defer it to refractory exit. SparkBrain therefore needs an explicit discard/defer/clamp/integrate contract rather than inferring semantics from the label alone.

Current-based LIF references algebraically combine excitatory and inhibitory currents while separately defining refractory voltage clamping. SparkBrain's production path uses ordinary signed-current netting followed by a custom negative-only refractory membrane update, so balanced excitation can cancel inhibition before the gate without any additional memory mechanism.

Standard generalized integrate-and-fire and simulator models allow different state variables to evolve or retain history across refractory intervals. A later probe-spike difference caused by a refractory-time input is therefore ordinary retained-state behavior unless a distinct residual remains after explicit state-policy controls.
sources: Jolivet et al., Generalized Integrate-and-Fire Models, Journal of Neurophysiology, DOI 10.1152/jn.00190.2004

findings.summary: Conductance-based neuron models compute E/I effects from membrane voltage and reversal potentials, and shunting-inhibition theory shows nonlinear excitation-inhibition interactions. Equal nominal positive/negative current cancellation is therefore specific to the current-based engineering abstraction and should not be generalized biologically.
sources: Tuckwell, On shunting inhibition, Biological Cybernetics 1986, DOI 10.1007/BF00341923
